#917. India fight back as New Zealand lose first home ODI series since 2019

India's Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj and Axar Patel make vital contributions with bat and ball as New Zealand lose home ODI series for first time since 2019; Kiwis had won 11 bilateral contests in a row on own turf before 3-1 defeat; teams now meet in two Tests, starting on November 19

India fought back to inflict a first home ODI series defeat on New Zealand since their own victory in the country in 2019 as they won a low-scoring fifth game in Mount Maunganui by 22 runs.

The visitors slumped to 34-3 - albeit better than the 0-3 where they found themselves during a 244-run thrashing in the fourth ODI at the same venue on Friday - and later lost four wickets for 23 runs to be bowled out for 209 after losing the toss at Bay Oval.

However, the 26 runs put on in partnership between last-wicket pair Arshdeep Singh (14) and Mohammed Siraj (14) proved crucial after that duo bagged five wickets between them - Arshdeep bagging 3-30 and Siraj 2-50 - to skittle the Black Caps for 187 in reply.

New Zealand had already seen India end their streak of 11 straight home bilateral ODI series victories but would have had the consolation of a 2-2 draw had they produced a successful chase and looked poised to do that before losing 5-55 from 64-1.

India's spin-bowling all-rounder Axar Patel followed his innings of 46 - he joint top-scored in the match alongside team-mate Ishan Kishan - with figures of 2-28 from 6.1 overs as the tourists claimed the series 3-1.

India 209 all out in 42.1 overs (put in to bat): Ishan Kishan (46), Axar Patel (46); Mitchell Santner (3-47), Jacob Duffy (3-60), Matt Fisher (2-28)

New Zealand 187 all out in 48.1 overs (target 210): Dean Foxcroft (31), Mitchell Santner (24), Nick Kelly (24); Arshdeep Singh (3-30), Axar Patel (2-28), Mohammed Siraj (2-50)

The Kiwis' woes began when Will Young (22) was caught off Arshdeep by Ruturaj Gaikwad at deep square, with top-scorer Dean Foxcroft (31) sixth out when he chopped Yash Thakur (1-38) onto his stumps to hand the India debutant his maiden ODI scalp.

Thakur's strike meant India claimed two wickets in as many balls, with Auqib Nabi removing Michael Bracewell (19) from the previous delivery, caught at deep midwicket.

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner (24) and Kristian Clarke (16) put on 39 for the seventh wicket from 119-6 but when Santner was out slog-sweeping Naman Dhir (1-4) and Clarke snicked Arshdeep behind, Axar polished off the tail.

New Zealand lost the preceding T20I series 3-2.

The Kiwis will now host India in two Tests, starting in Wellington on November 19 ahead of a second fixture in Christchurch from November 27.

#916. ‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts

Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players

Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to run at 81% of her max speed at 32 weeks pregnant.

Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for Angel City FC, documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, Millie Bright announced her pregnancy in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal.

“I think it’s becoming more common. You’re seeing it more often, especially in America,” says 32-year-old Emslie, who trained at high intensity throughout her pregnancy, with a three-person team looking after her. She gave birth to her son, Jamie, in December 2025 and returned to competitive action by May 2026; scoring her first goal since coming back for Scotland in October, and her first club goal this month. “It’s amazing what the body can do. I debunked a lot of myths that I’d heard about being pregnant.”

For many years, says the physiotherapist and Women’s Football Hub founder Carolyn Kent, there was huge caution around high-impact sports and pregnancy. The fear was that overexertion and physical contact – a heart rate going too high, a bad fall, a mistimed kick to the abdomen – could cause miscarriage. But slowly this is changing. In July Fifa launched its Stay in Play guidelines and research, which offer a groundbreaking framework for decision-making around football participation during pregnancy.

“I was always told that once you hit that first trimester, 12 weeks, all contact stops. But actually they’re now saying, no, we need to be a little bit more nuanced than that,” says Kent. The research suggests that while that timeframe should still be considered the loose recommended cut-off point for full-contact football (due to the uterus growing over the pubic bone and offering less protection for the growing foetus in the second trimester), low-contact and modified training can continue in the absence of any medical reason for it not to.

“Pregnancy does not mean game over,” adds Kent. “It does not mean that ‘OK, I’ve got to automatically stop’. That again feeds into this narrative that females are fragile. Your body’s amazing.”

Up to 2021, only 6% of sports science research was done on women, which means gaps are still being filled in. But as the women’s game continues to grow, this is happening at speed, says Sinéad Dufour, a pelvic health physiotherapist and academic who was one of the researchers who developed the Stay in Play guidelines. She gives Fifa credit for recognising the development of the women’s game – its popularity and intensity has soared in the past 10 years with more than six million women and girls playing football in England alone.

“More and more players are now staying through until they’re having families … And they put all this money into research,” she says. They have identified “clear cut” physical and mental health benefits for women to keep up with football, including a lower injury risk postpartum.

“There’s always been a notion that women just aren’t strong and robust the way we actually are, and now the science is proving otherwise,” Dufour says. “I do think some of it relates to the foetus. That’s going to supersede what’s actually good for the woman, right?”

Some of the main considerations players should have, whether professional or amateur, as to whether they should keep playing and training throughout pregnancy, relate to pain, pelvic floor dysfunction, and motor control and movement, she adds. But the decision whether or not to continue playing during pregnancy is ultimately personal.

When Emma Kelly, who plays for Newcastle, unexpectedly became pregnant earlier this year at the age of 29, she was anxious. She had never played with a pregnant teammate before and she had been out for much of the season due to injury. How isolating would the experience be? Was it going to jeopardise her career? “I was questioning whether this is the right time,” she says. “It’s not that I’m ungrateful but it’s just finding it hard being out of the team again and not being able to play the sport that I love.”

Though she continued to train, she and her partner decided she would stop contact football immediately, prior to 12 weeks, as “football is so unpredictable”, she says. As she didn’t want to announce her pregnancy until she was into the second trimester, in the interim she told her teammates that she was unwell. Like Emslie she has been documenting her training with the encouragement of her club and feels as if she is noticing more and more athletes doing the same. “I want to continue as long as my body allows me to,” she says. Her club has been “extremely supportive” with specialised training, physio and equipment.

But for all the newfound positivity around pre-and postpartum for footballers, Emslie says candidly, there are some hard truths that players have to face: namely that pregnancy is a sacrifice. The pitch is their stage and no player wants to be relegated to the role of understudy, relearning how to bend their body to their will. “If I wasn’t worried about [fertility], I wouldn’t have gotten pregnant till I was retired,” she says. “I could have had a full football career.”

The other is that football is a business. “You’re used as a player,” she says bluntly. “As soon as you turn a certain age, or if you’ve got a kid, they look at you different … As a player, you’re wanted until you’re not.” Though she made it clear she wasn’t talking about her own club, which was very supportive of her pregnancy and return, at the time of interview she was two months away from her contract ending with Angel City but had no news of a new deal being offered.

Even so, Dufour says, the body works hard during pregnancy; aerobic capacity is pushed. “The biggest stress test you’re ever going to go through is pregnancy,” she says. Her data shows that some women will achieve personal bests on their return. In short pregnancy could be a secret superpower. In an industry as capitalistic, brutal and data-driven as football, that’s an important fact.

#914. Life With Derek Star Says Actors “Leaned Into” Stepsibling Romance

Life With Derek’s Michael Seater revealed that he and costar Ashley Leggat were not only aware of romance rumors between their stepsibling characters, but they “leaned into” it on screen.

Nearly 15 years after Life With Derek concluded, the actor behind the titular Derek Venturi in show admitted he and onscreen stepsister Ashley Leggat—a.k.a. Casey McDonald—leaned into their characters’ flirty tension while filming the blended family comedy.

“We had an undeniable chemistry that the fans loved,” Seater recalled during a recent appearance on the Back to the Best podcast. “Enemies to lovers? Whatever the trope is? So, fans wanted that and we were like, ‘Well they’re step siblings so technically…’”

Seater and Leggat played not only stepsiblings, but characters who were always at odds with each other. However, while the Canadian sitcom was airing—it aired from 2005 to 2009 on the Family Channel in Canada in the Disney Channel in the U.S. before ending with a 2010 movie—many fans picked up on how the constant fire between their characters could easily burn into a romance.

And the actors didn’t let that speculation go unnoticed.

“In these early days of the internet, our producers don’t know there’s like forums online where people are talking but we do,” the 39-year-old explained. “So, we saw that the fans were talking about it. We knew that the fans liked it, so we leaned into it without letting the writers or producers know that we were leaning into it.”

And while Seater and Leggat, 40, were never actually romantically involved on the show, the showrunners and writers had to step in to keep them apart. As he shared of one take, “We’d be like sitting on a couch and they’d be like, ‘Can you maybe separate yourselves a little on the couch?’”

Of course, Seater stressed that while he loved the ‘will they, won’t they?’ that existed between Derek and Casey, the duo didn’t want the stepsiblings to canonically be together.

“The thing is, won’t they,” Seater continued, “but we’d tease them a little.”

Case in point: Remember that final scene in the finale where Derek appears to seduce Casey by emphasizing their stepsibling status? Seater teased, “I know what I’m doing there.”

Behind the camera, however, Seater and Leggat—who reprised their roles in the 2023 TV movie Life with Luca—have never been anything but great friends and scene partners.

“Ashley’s always my favorite scene partner honestly because I could always do anything,” he mused. “You felt so safe. In comedy, you want to be able to try stuff and play around and it’s not always going to land and if you have a scene partner that’s like, ‘Ew I don’t know about that. That wasn’t great.’ It makes you afraid to try things. It makes you self-conscious.”

As he put it, “We just always had each other’s backs and we were always just going with it.”

For more costars who never actually dated, keep reading...

The Anyone But You costars may have found love onscreen, but that's where it stayed. Despite the onslaught of dating rumors amid their 2023 press tour, the pair emphasized that their relationship was strictly platonic.

"The two things that you have to sell a rom-com are fun and chemistry," Powell told the New York Times in April 2024. "Sydney and I have a ton of fun together, and we have a ton of effortless chemistry. That's people wanting what's on the screen off the screen, and sometimes you just have to lean into it a bit—and it worked wonderfully. Sydney is very smart."

Meanwhile, Sweeney—who was engaged to businessman Jonathan Davino at the time, though they split in March 2025 after seven years together—asserted that she and Powell didn't play up their chemistry ahead of the rom-com's release.

"Honestly, the press did it themselves. There was no leaning in, per se," she told Variety in October 2025. "Truly, the tabloids and journalists just created it and kept going."

"Glen and I genuinely care for each other and have a love and respect for one another," the actress emphasized. "I love being with him. And I think people just truly saw a really beautiful pairing."

Hermione Granger and Draco Malfoy?! If Watson had it her way, the Harry Potter franchise would have had a Hogwarts House-crossed romance going down off-screen. The actress has admitted to nursing a serious crush on her bleached blonde costar.During the Harry Potter 20th anniversary special, Watson shared that as a child she "fell in love" with Felton while on the set of their first film together, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. "I used to come in every day and look for his number on the call sheet, it was No. 7, and if his name was on the call sheet, it was an extra exciting day," she said during the reunion. "He was three years above me and so for him he was like, 'You're like my little sister.'"Shortly after the special premiered, fans of the series quickly took to the Internet to share their wish for the longtime friends to become something more.However, in an interview with British Vogue, Watson addressed the online reaction and put any potential dating rumors to rest. "We speak most weeks," she said, "and we just think it's sweet."

The one where Ross and Rachel were almost each other's lobsters in real-life.During HBO Max's Friends reunion, Aniston and Schwimmer—who played one of TV's most beloved couples—explained that art reflected real life a bit during the show's first season. "At some point, we were both crushing hard on each other, but it was like two ships passing because one of us was always in a relationship, and we never crossed that boundary," Schwimmer said. "We respected that."Aniston added, "Honestly, I remember saying one time to David, 'It's going to be such a bummer if the first time you and I actually kiss is going to be on national television.' And sure enough, the first time we kissed was in that coffee shop."So, instead of having a romance IRL, she explained that they "just channeled all of our adoration and love for each other into Ross and Rachel."

Arguably one of the most iconic pairings in movie history, fans have shipped Leo and Kate together since 1996's Titanic (even though she didn't make room for him on that door). Still, they never let go of their friendship, with Winslet telling The Guardian that they are "bonded for life." From walking the red carpet together at the 1998 Golden Globes to watching DiCaprio blow kisses to Winslet during her emotional 2009 Golden Globes speech, it's so evident that the feelings between the besties have only continued to grow over the past two decades, iceberg be damned.

The unexpected pairing's chemistry in 2019's A Star Is Born and its ensuing press tour made fans blind to the fact that the actor was dating Irina Shayk and the "Bad Romance" singer was engaged to Christian Carano at the time.Still, it was clear that the costars had a close bond, with Gaga revealing that she had an "instant connection" with Cooper that came "the second that I saw him."Of course, that closeness was on full display when the pair took to the Oscars stage in 2019, hand-in-hand, to perform their Best Song-winning number, "Shallow," just days after Gaga ended her engagement.

But the House of Gucci star quickly shut down romance rumors following the performance, telling Jimmy Kimmel, "Yes, people saw love and—guess what—that's what we wanted you to see."Cooper, whose romance with Shayk ended later that year, never addressed the speculation until November 2021, telling The Hollywood Reporter they were acting during the Oscar performance."They kind of fall in love in that scene in the film," he explained. "It's that explosive moment that happens to them on a stage in front of thousands of people…It would have been so weird if we were both on stools facing the audience."

Gaga isn't the first costar Cooper has been romantically linked to in the press, with his onscreen dynamic with Lawrence in movies such as Silver Linings Playbook and American Hustle sparking rumors for years. In fact, Cooper was asked by Howard Stern in 2015, "When are you two gonna have sex? Everyone is waiting for that." The actor was quick to respond, "Never. It's just not the way we are together."And, at the 2013 Golden Globes, when he was asked by Entertainment Tonight if they were were dating, Cooper responded, "Oh my god. That's very funny. No, my God, no."

Since starring in Speed together in 1994, rumors have raced over the decades that Bullock and Reeves had an off-screen romance. Alas, it was never meant to me, with Sandra denying the two were ever a couple in an interview with Esquire magazine."Nope...but who knows?," she said. "Keanu's a guy who, I feel like, is friends with every woman he's ever dated. I don't think there's anyone who has something horrible to say about him. So maybe we could have survived. I don't know. But we didn't have to survive anything. We just get to grow up together on parallel roads and tip our hats and meet for a dinner and try to work together. And the longer time goes on, the more in awe I am of the human being. Would I have been able to say that if he had dumped me and made me angry? Probably not."Still, the duo, who also costarred in 2006's The Lake House, are close friends, with Bullock citing Reeves's listening skills as one of his best attributes. The Miss Congeniality star recalled that about a year after filming Speed, she casually mentioned to her costar that she'd never had champagne and truffles. A few days later, she told the outlet, Reeves hand-delivered those two items (and flowers), explaining, "I just thought you might want to try champagne and truffles, to see what it's like."

Moviegoers have Crazy, Stupid, Love for this pairing after they've played romantic interests in three films, including La La Land.Though they never dated in real life, working together forged a bond between the two actors. During a Q&A session at the 2018 Telluride Film Festival, the Cruella star revealed how much Gosling meant to her and his impact on her life and career. Calling him a "dear, wonderful friend," Stone said, "I can't even imagine what my life would be without Ryan. She then added, "He's so special. It makes me emotional."And before La La Land debuted in 2016, Stone joked around about the number of films she's done with Gosling, telling E! News, "He has a restraining order against me now.""Restraining order" aside, Gosling said it was "great to work" with Emma, explaining, "I think it brings the best out of [us] because you know one another, and you are able to help each other in a way that you can't if you're strangers."

Jim and Pam on The Office are one of the most beloved TV couples of all-time, with fans rooting for the Dunder Mifflin employees to be together throughout the NBC hit's nine-year run. Jam's chemistry never transitioned into an off-screen romance between John and Jenna, though she did admit to the pair having "real chemistry" during a 2016 appearance on Watch What Happens Live when a caller asked how close they were."There's like a real part of me that is Pam and a real part of him that's Jim and those parts of us were genuinely in love with one another," Fischer explained. "But in real life we aren't totally Pam and totally Jim, so in real life we're not the perfect match…he was like a type of spouse that I had for a long time, he was my partner and we will always be close because of it."Krasinski later weighed in on his costar's headline-making comments, telling The Daily Beast, "I think we both feel it's such an honor to be a part of that relationship. As far as how she was quoted about saying we were 'genuinely in love,' I think that was taken wildly out of context and I feel bad for her."We'll always have the teapot.

They may have costarred in How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, but the pair gained a rapid number of fans rooting for them to find each other IRL after the 2006 rom-com. But it never happened.In an interview with Howard Stern on his SiriusXM show in October 2020, McConaughey revealed it simply never appealed to him to date one of his famous costars."I've always tried to keep it professional and the people I worked with, I must say, did it well," he shared. "Maybe we had certain crushes on each other at certain times but we always just kept it professional."

And with that, the chance for their love to blossom died, just like that love fern.

These A-list best friends have off-the-charts on-screen chemistry (Ocean's Eleven, anyone?) that has extended offscreen in a purely platonic way. Just look at their giggle-filled interviews, gushing public speeches and the fact that George has lent out his coveted Lake Como home to the Roberts-Moder family for anniversary celebrations. NBD!

Along with the ball dropping on New Year's Eve, you can always count on people wondering if the best friends and CNN's Live From Times Square co-hosts have ever dated. When Cohen appeared on Howard Stern's radio show, he was asked, "What is it about Anderson Cooper that keeps you from falling in love with him?" The Watch What Happens Live host replied, "I just think it's not what our relationship is based on. We're just friends. That's not a part of it. I think, at this point, we know each other too well. We're not attracted to each other in that way."Funnily enough, the pair first met when they were set up on a blind date over 25 years ago. "You know when straight people know two gay guys, they're like, 'Oh, you guys should meet,'" Cooper said on The Tonight Show in 2017, adding that when the two had a phone call to schedule the date, he "knew within 45 seconds I was never going on a date with Andy Cohen."He explained that Cohen "violated" a cardinal rule" when it comes to dating the CNN host: He asked about Anderson's mother, Gloria Vanderbilt. "I wanted to date the Vanderbilt boy!" Cohen admitted. "I was excited!"

While Deschanel said the pair had "so much fun" making the 2009 indie rom-com (500) Days of Summer, Gordon-Levitt admitted dating his costar and longtime friend would be "awkward" in a 2012 interview with Playboy."Zooey and I just think it's funny," he said of fans wanting them to be together. "It is funny. We've been friends for 10 years."

Before it was confirmed that the High School Musical heartthrob was dating his costar Vanessa Hudgens, there was speculation that he was involved with their mutual best friend Tisdale. His 2006 guest appearance as her love interest on The Suite Life of Zack and Cody only fueled the rumors.Efron and Tisdale still remain close to this day, with the latter calling him her "brother/best friend," though she did pick him as her worst onscreen kiss in an interview with Elle. "It was the worst because he is like my brother," Tisdale explained. "At the time, he was used to acting on Warner Brothers, which is CW, and we were on Disney Channel."She then called him out for trying to kiss her "with his tongue," prompting her to tell him, "'Get away from me!'""I closed my mouth so fast. I was like, 'This is Disney Channel, we don't kiss like that on Disney Channel!'" Tisdale recalled. "It's just weird when you're so close to somebody, we'd already done a movie, I'd known him for years before,'" she said. "'That is why it was the worst, it's just we're too close.'"

While their High School Musical characters Chad and Taylor were teen sweethearts, Bleu and Coleman left the Disney franchise with a lifelong friendship. The duo reunited onscreen in the 2021 Lifetime Christmas movie, A Christmas Dance Reunion, with Bleu writing on Instagram, "After 13 years it felt like coming home working and dancing with [Monique] again. Starring in a [Lifetime] Christmas movie has always been a dream of mine, but never in a million years did I think I'd get to share the screen with one of my favorite people."And Coleman is hoping to continue working with "one of her best friends," telling People, "I honestly pray that we get to do more things together because we have that sort of spark that Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan had, and Leo and Kate, and Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, and all of these different couples that we've seen in movie after movie together. I really feel like we have that potential as well and I'd like to see that happen."

They may have played one of TV's most iconic will-they-or-won't-they couples on The X-Files, but the costars actually didn't get along while filming their hit Fox show. In a 2008 interview with Metro UK, Duchovny admitted that he often fought with Anderson during the series' initial eight-year run because, "Familiarity breeds contempt. It's nothing to do with the other person. We used to argue about nothing. We couldn't stand the sight of each other."That didn't stop fans from wanting Mulder and Scully to get together, both on-screen and off, with a photo from their May 2021 lunch date going viral, much to Duchovny's amusement. "As I was leaving she was like, 'Let's take a photo,'" he told People. "I was told there was a big reaction to it! I never get that stuff, but it's really cool that people are interested after all these years."

Avengers shippers, assemble!While they've appeared in nine movies together since first collaborating on 2004's The Perfect Score, the superhero costars have never hooked up IRL. But Evans and Johansson have developed a deep comfort level with each other over the years. "It's really a result of 10 years of knowing somebody," Johansson explained of their chemistry to Entertainment Weekly in March 2020, "and being able to have a kind of intimacy with them that I think you get from just spending a lot of time with somebody and knowing their soft underbelly."

#912. Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United

Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team

Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final. His presence lifted those clubs.

However, the Argentinian has competed in only one of the past six Premier League campaigns. Winning Ligue 1 and the Coupe de France in an 18-month spell with Paris Saint-Germain tells us little. His most pertinent recent experience for the Manchester United job is the 2023-24 season he spent at Chelsea, a campaign that left more questions than answers.

The club had finished 12th the season before, in the first year of the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital era. Pochettino was always likely to take Chelsea higher. And he did. But his influence is harder to judge. Opta predicted Chelsea would finish sixth in 2023-24, a forecast that proved correct. By this measure Pochettino hit par though, as Transfermarkt rated the market value of his squad as the third-highest in the Premier League in October 2023, perhaps he fell short.

The squad value grew thanks to remarkable investment. Chelsea spent more than any other club in Europe’s big five leagues in each of the three transfer windows from the summer of 2022 to the summer of 2023. Working for Boehly will have provided a good primer for the madness of Manchester United, even if the spending won’t be as generous.

Assembling a winning team from a rapidly evolving squad is not easy. Pochettino crafted a side that delivered the fifth-most expected points in 2023-24. Chelsea’s 63.4 was a fair way shy of Arsenal (81.2), Manchester City (79.3) and Liverpool (76.2) but it was a decent first season.

Chelsea conceded 63 league goals, the club’s worst figure in the Premier League era. Yet only twice have they amassed more than the 77 goals they scored. They were a little above their expected goal figures at each end but the bulk of their large goal totals was reflected in the underlying data.

But even the xG numbers raised questions, because Chelsea benefited from 12 penalties, the joint-second-most in the past 10 Premier League seasons. Chelsea have had 14 in their 86 league games since Pochettino left. They conceded five penalties and committed the joint-most Opta-defined defensive errors leading to shots (22) in Pochettino’s season.

Across three matches in April 2024 they drew 2-2 with the bottom side Sheffield United, thumped Everton 6-0 then lost 5-0 at Arsenal. They endured a similar seesaw sequence earlier in the campaign, losing 4-1 at Tottenham and Newcastle, with a 4-4 draw against Manchester City in between. Chelsea also set the record for matches in which a team score and concede at least two goals in a 38-game Premier League season (12). How do you assess a manager’s performance in that maelstrom?

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

If the low point was not the Arsenal loss, it was being called “billion-pound bottle jobs” by Gary Neville after losing the 2024 Carabao Cup final. Never mind that Chelsea had enough chances to win, Pochettino had to answer for the defeat. Less than three months later, he was gone.

The Premier League has evolved in Pochettino’s relatively brief absence. Arne Slot arrived, won the title and left, while Guardiola’s departure leaves no big managerial beasts remaining. There have been tactical shifts, with increased man-to-man marking across the pitch, and set-piece skirmishes have decided more matches than feels healthy.

Opta’s data shows Pochettino’s probable new side move upfield more quickly but press less intensely than his Chelsea team. There will need to be an adjustment. But can a manager whose training methods at Chelsea were described by a well-placed source as “antiquated” get up to speed as quickly as United need?

Pochettino will adapt and his Premier League record commands the utmost respect. The relevance of his recent work to United in 2026-27 is less clear.

#911. Jodie Foster Makes Rare Comment on Family Life With Sons Charlie & Kit

Hexed's Jodie Foster detailed the parenting lesson she's learned as mom to sons Charles “Charlie” Bernard Foster, 28, and Christopher “Kit” Bernard Foster, 25, in an exclusive E! News interview.

Jodie Foster will never silence her lambs.

In fact, the Hexed star encourages her sons Charles “Charlie” Bernard Foster, 28, and Christopher “Kit” Bernard Foster, 25, to explore their passions.

"Being a mother of two boys, you learn the lesson of that they have to discover things for themselves," Foster exclusively told E! News' Lauren Herbert at the Los Angeles premiere of her new Disney movie Nov. 12, "and that you can't protect them and that you have to just be positive for their life choices."

The 63-year-old continued, "If they make a mistake, they make one and you just hope that they learn from it instead of intervening."

But for Foster—who shares her kids with ex Cydney Bernard—that's a parenting lesson she didn't need to pass on to her costar Hailee Steinfeld, who gave birth to daughter Harper with husband Josh Allen in April.

As the Oscar winner put it, "She is mama extraordinaire."

"It's so incredible that Hailee did this movie, first, pregnant," Foster raved, "and then holding the baby, basically."

What's more, watching Steinfeld, 29, experience many motherhood firsts brought back fond memories for Foster and their castmate Rashida Jones, who's mom to 8-year-old son Isaiah with longtime partner Ezra Koenig.

"All of the feelings and thoughts that were going through her mind at that time, realizations about her own mother and how she'd been parented, I remember that when my kids were little," Foster shared. "It's like we're all of the different eras."

But Foster also experienced a personal first while working on Hexed: playing a Disney villain.

"I've always wanted to be a villain," she said. "Now, I get to be a Disney villain, which is the most special thing, because this one is very grounded. It, in some ways, feels like somebody that you could know and weirdly, that makes it more emotional and special."

Disney's Hexed is out in theaters Nov. 25.

For more stars sharing their motherhood journeys, keep reading.

The Oscar winner, who has worked with organizations like UNICEF and is a UN Goodwill Ambassador, makes it a priority to share those same humanitarian values with her six children.

"With my family, I'm trying to raise them to have respect for all people and make friends around the world and feel at home with the world and really live a truly global [life]," she told NBC News in 2011. "I think it's what forms them and it's really important to me."

"I know it’s cliché, but I love everything, even the hard parts," the Kardashians star—mom to daughter True and son Tatum with ex Tristan Thompson—said of motherhood in a 2022 interview with Elle. "[My kids] challenge me as a person, and being able to shape little people into really incredible big people is an honor and a gift."

"We have to take those roles seriously, especially in today’s day and age, with how much accessibility children have and the information they’re exposed to so young," she added. "It’s super scary, but I take my job very seriously. I love it so much."

"I have such unconditional love for my kids," the Keep Up With the Kardashians alum—who shares North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm with ex-husband Kanye West—wrote on her website in 2017. "No matter what, I will always love them and support them in anything they choose to do in life."

"My family was so close growing up; now that I'm a mom, I understand the bond my mom and dad felt with us," she continued. "There can be ups and downs with kids but no matter what, I always learn so much from them. Being a mom is the most important job I have."

In a 2018 interview, the Kylie Cosmetics founder shared how much her mindset has changed since giving birth to Stormi that year.

"I think more about the future because of her. Every time I leave and I'm stressed about leaving her, I'm like, ‘I'm doing it for you,'" Kylie—who also shares son Aire with ex Travis Scott—told London Evening Standard. "Everyone says you change completely when you become a mom, but I really feel the same, just better."

The Poosh creator shares kids Mason, Penelope and Reign with ex Scott Disick. She's also mom to son Rocky with husband Travis Barker.

"It's definitely my favorite role in life," she said of motherhood in a 2012 interview with Parents. "It has changed me and made me realize there is nothing else I would rather do with my time. Being a mom is what life is about. I hope people realize what the priorities in life should be and know not everything has to be perfect."

As mom to kids Camden, Jaxon and Saylor with ex Jay Cutler, the Laguna Beach alum told Modeliste Magazine in 2016, "There's just so much more love in your life. I finally feel like I have a real identity"

"I feel like I have a purpose here in life now," she added. "I'm a mom to these three amazing little babies, and my whole world just kind of opened up."

"As soon as I found out I was pregnant," the Pretty Little Liars actress—who shares daughters Atlas and Rome with Matte Babel—said in a 2023 interview with Byrdie, "I put the old version of myself aside, and a new chapter began."

"I never want my children to say I work too much," she continued. "When I'm putting them to bed or having a meal with them, I put my phone down. They're growing up so quickly, and I don't want to look back and think, 'I missed this because of a work function.'"

The Lizzie McGuire alum is mom to son Luca with her ex-husband Mike Comrie. she also shares daughters Banks, Mae and Townes with husband Matthew Koma.

"I don't always balance it all," she admitted of her parenting duties in a 2018 interview with E! News, "I do the best that I can, and some months are crazier than others."

Still, Duff considers herself "a mother first."

"My decision-making process is like, 'Hey can I make this work?'" she said of finding family time in her busy work life. "I've been doing this for a while so I do have a strong work ethic, and I have a lot of people around me that help keep my schedule straight and plan and know where my priorities lie."

The powerhouse singer is a huge inspiration to all of us, but turns out the mother of Blue, Rumi and Sir—who she shares with husband Jay-Z—also makes sure to be the same for her own children.

"It just gives you purpose and all of the things that my self-esteem was associated it, it's all completely different," she said of motherhood in a 2012 interview with Anderson Cooper. "I realized why I was born and more than anything all of the things I want to pass onto my child and the best way of doing that is not by preaching or telling her but showing her by example."

For the Devil Wears Prada star, becoming a mom was a groundbreaking experience in both personal and work life.

“I don't think it's necessary to be a mother to play a mother. I think that should be open to lots of different actors," she told People in 2024, adding that welcoming sons Jonathan and Jack with husband Adam Shulman helped her gain an understanding of "the depth of love" maternal characters can feel.

The Mindy Project actress—who is mom to kids Katherine, Spencer and Anne—said she feels "so much more happy and confident after having children."

"In each subsequent year of my life, I'm just feeling happier and happier," she told ABC News in 2021, "and I am amazed at that,"

Though she played one of the titular Bad Moms in the 2016 comedy, the actress couldn't be a better parent to her kids Wyatt and Dimitri, who she shares with Ashton Kurcher.

"I reprioritized my life, in all honesty," Kunis said of her motherhood journey in a 2016 interview with Entertainment Tonight. "I traveled through all my 20s and I was very selfish—in a good way, not in a way I regret. And I think having a kid made me realize how incredibly selfless I want to be."

The Transformers actress—who shares kids Noah, Bodhi and Journey with her ex-husband Brian Austin Green, as well as daugther Saga with ex-fiancé Machine Gun Kelly—has a lovely approach to her parenting style.

"I don't think I need to teach my children with harsh words or with punishment. I believe that if I love them the right way, there's no need for that," she told Harper's Bazaar Arabia in 2015. "I'm a free-spirit mother."

The Gossip Girl alum and Ryan Reynolds' couple goals include being amazing parents to four children, including all the funny moments that come with being a parent.

"It's tough when you get pooped on and barfed on, but having a baby is wonderful," Lively joked to NW Magazine in 2016. "Even when it's tough and I'm exhausted, I think, 'I am so fortunate.'"

#909. 'I can't believe he is one of us' - inside Salah's life in Trabzon

Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor

Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans.

That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers after the expiry of his Liverpool contract, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear.

"The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too.

From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown.

"I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us."

Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him.

At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else.

Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival.

"Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel.

The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier.

Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival.

On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg.

"He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud.

At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million.

Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination.

The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions.

Trabzonspor trail leaders Galatasaray by three points, having won seven of their first 10 games, including victories against the table-toppers and Besiktas.

For context, the Istanbul 'big three' of Galatasaray (26), Fenerbahce (19) and Besiktas (16) have won the league on 61 occasions combined, compared with Trabzonspor's seven titles.

"In Turkey, he is the biggest football star after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo," says Kerim Tonyali, who is part of Gurbetci Gencler, a Trabzonspor supporters' group.

And given Salah's status as an icon, Trabzonspor are quickly becoming the second club for many in Turkey and the wider Muslim world.

Salah's face is a common sight wherever you go in Trabzon

Trabzon may be more than 2,000 miles from Liverpool but there are similarities, particularly when it comes to the sense of identity and pride associated with originating from here.

"Everywhere is Trabzon for us," is the local mantra and aligns with the sense of unity within this city that has a population of about 800,000 and is only the 30th-biggest in Turkey.

For Salah, the financials were important and he is earning about Â£14.6m per year as well as 20% of official merchandise sold with his name on, but one of the key aspects of coming here was the ability to focus entirely on his football.

Besiktas was considered as an option after the 2026 World Cup but, after multiple calls with Trabzonspor, Salah felt they were the ideal fit and offered a life away from the hustle and bustle of Istanbul.

He has his own security detail and is living in the nearby town of Yomra, where he now has a street named after him. He also employs a private chef and, unsurprisingly, continues to set standards in the gym and on the training ground.

By all accounts, Salah is thriving. He is a fan of Turkish coffee and is often spotted leaving the ground with Ayran - a traditional yogurt drink - but as much as he wants to explore the city, he knows of the difficulties given his reputation.

"Everyone wants to work with a star like Mohamed Salah," said Trabzonspor's Paul Onuachu, formerly of Southampton. "He adds so much and helps all of us and he contributes positively. I am grateful for him. It's a blessing to play with him."

Watching Salah in the flesh in a Conference League game against Freiburg, his pace has gone down a notch compared with his peak but the touch, quick feet and sheer quality is still there. And so is that knack of getting in goalscoring positions, even if his defensive duties - which were such a source of debate last season at Liverpool - are limited.

Salah believes he still has plenty to give for club and country, with aspirations to play in both the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and 2030 World Cup, which will be partly held in North Africa.

No decision has been made about how long he will stay in Turkey, but there is growing belief among sources in the Middle East that he will move to Saudi Arabia when his two-year Trabzonspor deal expires in 2028. By then, he will be 36.

Salah signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor in the summer of 2026

On initial thoughts, it is easy to question how and why Salah ended up here.

When he delivered that infamous mixed-zone interview at Leeds' Elland Road less than a year ago and the wheels of his departure from Liverpool were set in motion, surely no-one would have imagined his next destination would be this Turkish outpost near the Georgian border.

"I remember looking at him when we landed in Trabzon and seeing the crowds outside and how emotional it was," says Anil Dincer, one of the lawyers involved in Salah's move to Turkey.

"We already have Salah and Fabinho. So now we are waiting for [Virgil] Van Dijk," adds Serhat Sumer, a Trabzonspor fan.

Salah, of course, delivered so much joy to Liverpool and the intention here is the same. This is no drift towards retirement, but a player determined to prove he still belongs at the highest level and that football still has meaning beyond trophies and money.

Asked by BBC Sport if he had a message for Liverpool fans, Salah simply said "hello" and smiled. Given how rarely he spoke in the mixed zone during his time at Anfield, it is not in his nature to talk regularly on record.

Last season was Salah's least prolific at Anfield, but given Liverpool's struggles in front of goal in the Premier League, it is hard to argue they have replaced one of their greatest ever players.

Perhaps a time will come when the likes of Salah, Arne Slot and Richard Hughes will reveal more about the chain of events that led to the forward agreeing to terminate his contract a year early. As it is, none of them are at the club and that chapter is firmly closed.

Salah's influence that once helped shape the Premier League is now being felt on the shores of the Black Sea. He is Trabzonspor's force of nature. And the team known as the Black Sea Storm are rising and on the hunt for silverware with their Egyptian King.

A rock in the Trabzon highlands became a tourist destination after Salah's visit

#908. Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?

The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years

There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him.

The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7.

“According to our latest evaluation, his brand alone is worth €850m (£710m),” he says. “People identify with his story: a young boy who travelled to Lisbon alone, lost his father and achieved success through his own hard work. Portugal has a long history of great players but no one has ever enjoyed this kind of global exposure. From a marketing standpoint, I have absolutely no doubt that most of the world watched Portugal’s matches because of Cristiano Ronaldo.”

Leonel Pontes, the technical director at Shanghai Shenhua, sees this reality in his everyday life. Pontes played an important role in shaping Ronaldo’s career at Sporting’s academy and became a mentor, helping the teenager from Madeira to cope with homesickness. He later coached Ronaldo as Portugal’s assistant manager and has been in China since 2023.

“When I tell people here in China that I’m Portuguese, the first thing they talk about is Cristiano,” Pontes says. “Just earlier this week, I visited an exhibition about his career here in Shanghai. I think his departure from the national team, which was always going to happen sooner or later, wasn’t handled properly. There were mistakes on both sides [by the player and the coach] but the country missed an opportunity to pay tribute to everything he has given us.”

So, what do the national team, who host Denmark in Braga, have left? A wealth of talent, certainly. Vitinha, Bruno Fernandes, João Neves, Nuno Mendes and Diogo Costa are some of the most prominent names in a squad packed with technical quality and tactical intelligence.

Petit, who played with Ronaldo for Portugal between 2003 and 2008 and manages the Azores club Santa Clara, says that talent must take responsibility. “Ronaldo could single-handedly solve a difficult game inside the box, with a free-kick or with another set piece. We, as teammates, were aware of it. But now we have great players from top clubs, they need to stand up. For some of them, this could be their last chance [for international success]. We are getting some younger players now. But Portugal has style and game ideas to be able to reach success.”

Replacing Ronaldo will mean more than finding someone capable of scoring his goals or wearing the No 7 shirt. He has been part of what it has meant to support Portugal. Fans grew up watching him, celebrating with him and, through the disappointments and triumphs, believing their national team could achieve something extraordinary with him leading the way. The country will move on but the era he leaves behind will be extraordinarily difficult to replicate.

Pontes, who assisted Paulo Bento with Portugal between 2010 and 2014, says: “He sacrificed a great deal for the national team. He played injured, he played when he wasn’t fully fit, but he was always there. He always gave his best.”

Ronaldo’s commitment to the game and love for Portugal was clear to Dany Mota, a Monza forward who trained with him at Juventus and with the national team. “When I arrived at Juventus, I had already heard the saying: ‘First to arrive at the training ground, last to leave.’ I wanted to see it for myself. So, one morning, I arrived really early, went to the gym, and there he was, already working out. After a few particularly demanding days, you would naturally start to feel a little tired or less motivated but that never seemed to happen to him. He would still be swimming, running or lifting weights in the gym. He was a machine and had an endless love for the national team.”

Portugal were blessed with talent before Ronaldo but major honours remained elusive. The so-called Golden Generation, featuring Luís Figo, Rui Costa and João Pinto, reached the semi-finals of Euro 2000 and, with a young Ronaldo, the final of Euro 2004, only to fall short. For Portugal supporters, there was a growing feeling that if the country was to triumph, it had to be with Ronaldo leading the way. He used defeat by Greece in the Euro 2004 final, on home soil, as fuel.

“He had a very particular ability to turn frustration into a desire to improve,” says Maniche, who shared the dressing room with Ronaldo during Portugal’s greatest football disappointment. “That characteristic has stayed with him throughout his career. Talent can open many doors, but it is that mentality that allows you to remain at the top for so many years.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

After Ronaldo’s 2004 tears of disappointment came tears of joy 12 years later when Portugal won the Euros in arguably the defining moment of his international career. Ronaldo was forced off injured against France but from the sidelines he encouraged his teammates, celebrated every intervention and experienced the final with the intensity of someone who understood what victory would mean to his country.

Millions around the world have identified deeply with Ronaldo’s journey. He embodies the fact that, regardless of where you come from or how difficult your circumstances, dedication, self-belief and an unwavering determination can take you further than anyone might have imagined. From a modest upbringing, with a father battling alcoholism, he has reached the pinnacle of football.

“When I first took him to the airport so he could fly back to Madeira for Christmas, I was afraid he wouldn’t come back,” Pontes recalls. “But he did. I’ve coached a lot of kids but Cristiano had two qualities I’d never seen in anyone else. First, he had a natural leadership ability and an extraordinary influence over his teammates, driven by his technical quality and fearlessness. Second, he possessed an exceptional mechanical understanding of his own body. He knew exactly how to position himself to achieve what he wanted, whether that meant adjusting his movement or striking the ball.”

At 41, his club career – with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia – has no end in sight. What still drives him, apart from the objective of scoring 1,000 career goals?

“It is a competitive mentality deeply ingrained in his personality,” Maniche says. “It is about the challenge of continuing to prove to yourself that you are good enough, that you can push beyond your own limits and sustain an extraordinary level of performance.”

Portugal did the extraordinary with Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?

#907. England level ODI series with Australia as Banton and Atkinson fire

Tom Banton scores second ODI ton as England hit record 355-6 in Australia before Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker reduce home side to 29-4; Mitch Marsh's hosts - who rested Mahli Beardman following six-wicket haul in the series opener - now meet England in winner-takes-all clash on Wednesday

Tom Banton's second ODI hundred and Gus Atkinson's sizzling new-ball burst saw England thump Australia by 135 runs in Adelaide and set up a series decider in Hobart on Wednesday.

A touring side rolled for 131 in Friday's opener at Perth posted their highest ODI total in Australia, with a score of 355-6 underpinned by Banton's 121 from 99 balls and featuring fifties for Jordan Cox (67 off 49), Joe Root (62 off 68) and Will Jacks (54no off 40).

England lost their fourth wicket in the 35th over - Banton holing out immediately after back-to-back sixes - whereas Australia lost their fourth at the end of the seventh with just 29 runs on the board, before being dismissed for 220 in 44.3 overs with Atkinson claiming 4-28 and Jofra Archer (1-26) taking the final wicket.

England 355-6 after 50 overs (put in to bat): Tom Banton (121 off 99 balls), Jordan Cox (67 off 49), Joe Root (62 off 68), Will Jacks (54no off 40); Xavier Bartlett (3-72)

Australia 220 all out in 44.3 overs (target 356): Cameron Green (64 off 82), Matt Renshaw (63 off 74); Gus Atkinson (4-28), Sam Curran (2-38), Liam Dawson (2-41)

The ODI finale at Ninja Stadium in Tasmania next week (3.30am start UK on Wednesday) is now winner-takes-all, ahead of the sides moving on to a five-match T20 international series, starting at the Melbourne Cricket Ground next Saturday (8.15am UK time).

In Sunday's match, Australia were reeling on 13-3 after three wickets for no runs in six balls as Atkinson had Travis Head (7) and Cooper Connolly (0) caught at slip in the same over before captain Mitchell Marsh (2) perished the same way off Sonny Baker (1-45).

When Josh Inglis (3) became the fourth man caught behind, off Atkinson after a successful review, Marsh's men looked to have little hope of completing their highest successful run chase at home.

Matt Renshaw (63) and Cameron Green (64) rebuilt with a fifth-wicket stand of 98, during which Renshaw was dropped on 27 by Jacks at cover and Green inexplicably grassed on seven at deep midwicket by Liam Dawson (2-41), the player who eventually broke the partnership when he pinned Renshaw lbw on the reverse sweep.

Green went on to be stumped in bizarre fashion as a delivery from Dawson ricocheted off wicketkeeper Cox's pads and back onto the stumps, while Sam Curran (2-38) was on a hat-trick after ousting Jack Edwards (17) with a moon ball and then Xavier Bartlett (0).

With the ball, Australia missed Mahli Beardman, who ripped through the away side with 6-24 at Optus Stadium two days earlier but was rested on Sunday, with the hosts taking a cautious approach with a quick whose young career has been hit by injury.

Banton is likely to line up in the middle order in the T20 series but has seemingly cinched a long-term spot in the ODI XI as opener after yet another impressive showing.

The Somerset batter has registered two hundreds and four fifties in nine innings since replacing the injured Jacob Bethell (knee) as Ben Duckett's top-order partner at the back end of the home summer, with this latest ton coming from a brisk 85 deliveries.

Banton was struck on the grille by a sharp bouncer from Beardman's replacement Riley Meredith early in his innings but he brushed off that blow to club many of his 16 boundaries (12 fours, four sixes) leg-side off the short deliveries Australia targeted him with.

Banton put on 137 with Root from 19-1, after Duckett clothed to point, and it was somewhat of a surprise when Root, perhaps looking to up the run rate, top-edged spinner Connolly into the off-side on the pull having been typically calm before then.

When England skipper Harry Brook (5) chopped on trying to scoop Meredith over fine leg and Banton's fine innings came to a close following a diving catch from Green in the deep, the visitors could have wobbled - but they didn't as the lower middle order fired.

Cox and Jacks dug in initially, before helping their team plunder 110 runs from the final 10 overs, a passage of play in which Curran (14 off 9) chipped in and Atkinson (13no off 4) belted Edwards for two sixes in an 18-run 50th over that concluded with a Jacks four.

It was then over to Atkinson and Baker with the ball - the latter given the new pill ahead of Archer - as Australia's top four each fell for single digits after playing flat-footed swats against back-of-a-length deliveries.

Their departures meant the result never looked in significant doubt and if England's catching had been on point - Root also dropped Inglis on one at slip - the margin of victory would have been even steeper.

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"I think we put in a really good performance there and it was really pleasing to see us bounce back [from the heavy defeat in Perth].

"We looked in control throughout the whole batting innings, countering their bad balls and putting them under pressure when we needed to.

"Banton played an exceptional innings, sticking to his strengths, and the depth we have means we were able to go on and get 350.

"[In the field], this is the template we want to set in every game. Bar a few dropped catches, it was awesome.

"A massive discussion in the group for a year and a half has been about wanting to be one of the best fielding sides in the world, one of the fittest and strongest sides in the world."

Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, speaking at the presentation:

"We bowled first thinking there might be a little bit in the wicket - which sounds weird to say at Adelaide Oval - and to maximise the first 20 overs, but England batted really well.

"I thought we tried a lot with the ball, a few different plans, like Riley Meredith bowling bumpers, but we knew England are a well-rounded side and they showed that today.

"With the bat, when you are chasing 350, you are under the pump from ball one and we needed two of the top four to go big and lay a platform."

ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time

#906. England's Blues brothers - how the Bellinghams helped save Birmingham

Jude Bellingham shared an old photo of him and brother Jobe after England's squad announcement last week

It is six years since Jude Bellingham played his final game for Birmingham City, and three years since younger brother Jobe wore the club's shirt for the last time.

While Jude, 23, is establishing himself as a footballing great at European greats Real Madrid following a spell at Borussia Dortmund, Jobe, 21, is continuing his football education at his brother's former club in Germany after two seasons with Sunderland.

The Stourbridge-born midfielders have moved on with their careers.

Their memories, however, live on at St Andrew's, such was the impact the boyhood Birmingham fans made in the Championship.

On match days supporters stop and pose for photographs in front of Jude's mural outside the ground. Fans still turn up to matches wearing Bellingham shirts.

"They both had a real connection with fans," Craig Courtney, from the Tilton Talk fan podcast, told BBC Sport. "Fans loved the fact they both cared.

"They wore their hearts on their sleeves and helped Birmingham when we were fighting relegation. Even now, Jude and Jobe remember where it all started for them."

The brothers played 70 league and cup games between them for Birmingham after graduating from the academy.

They have never appeared together in a senior match, however, as Jude - who joined Birmingham aged eight - had left by the time Jobe broke into the first team in 2022.

The Bellinghams will become the first brothers to play for England for 19 years if Jobe wins his first cap and appears alongside Jude, a veteran of 60 appearances, in the Nations League game with Croatia at Wembley.

"It will be an incredibly proud moment for Birmingham City if that happens," said Courtney.

'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up

Listen: How Jude Bellingham became a global brand

Birmingham supporters have had little to cheer about recently.

It is 15 years since they last appeared in the Premier League, while the 2011 League Cup winners even dipped down to League One recently.

While fierce rivals Aston Villa were playing - and beating - Bayern Munich and Bologna in the Champions League two years ago, Birmingham were losing at Shrewsbury and drawing with Northampton Town.

After 15 games Birmingham sit top of the Championship and there are plans for a new 62,000-capacity stadium in time for 2030-31.

"As a club, we've been right down in the doldrums," added Courtney. "Now we're top of the table and having a new stadium built.

"There is an argument that none of this would have been possible without the fees received for Jude and Jobe."

A mural tribute to Jude Bellingham outside St Andrew's

Jude is the youngest player in Birmingham's history after making his debut aged 16 years and 38 days in 2019.

Clubs across Europe were pursuing him when he signed his first professional contact in 2020 after turning 17 - a deal both he and Birmingham knew would never be fulfilled.

His actions, however, ensured Birmingham would receive a significant transfer fee when he left, and soon afterwards he joined Dortmund for an initial fee of Â£20m during the Covid-19 pandemic.

When he joined Real in 2023, Birmingham received a reported sell-on fee of at least Â£10m., external

"We cannot possibly imagine, without Jude's decision [to sign a contract], where we would be as a club in a pandemic like this," then Birmingham chief executive Xuandong Ren told BBC WM after Jude joined Dortmund.

"He could easily have just looked after himself and not the club, but he chose the best possible way to look after the club."

Jobe became the second youngest player to play for Birmingham when he made his debut in January 2022 aged 16 years and 107 days.

"This was a lad, regardless of who his brother was or what he was achieving, who would do anything to write his own success story," former Birmingham striker Troy Deeney, who played in the game when Jobe made his debut, told the Sun., external

"Everything he has achieved on the pitch, too, has come with an instant comparison to his older brother.

"He never got that one moment to enjoy something without someone, somewhere saying: 'Yeah, but what about Jude?'

"That only added to how strong he was mentally, and anyone who suggests he is where he is because of his last name is talking rubbish."

Deeney added: "What impressed me more than anything he had done on the pitch was his attitude - a hell-bent determination to get to the top and the common sense to take all the right steps along the way."

Jobe played 26 games before Sunderland paid Â£3m for him in 2023, with Birmingham receiving a reported Â£4m sell-on fee when he moved to Dortmund two years later.

Although significantly less than the fees generated by his brother, it was nevertheless welcome revenue.

Jobe Bellingham was given his Birmingham City debut by manager Lee Bowyer in January 2022

Both Jude and Jobe have returned to St Andrew's since their transfers.

Jobe captained England Under-21s to a 2-0 win against the Republic of Ireland at his old ground last November.

Before that match U21s boss Lee Carsley, who managed Jude when he was England interim manager in 2024, praised the brothers for their work ethic and determination to be the best.

Carsley said: "I know how much they love the Blues still and how important the club is to them."

Jude, tipped to be a future England captain, was at St Andrew's in July watching his former club in a pre-season friendly against Barcelona. He even wore a Birmingham shirt while watching from the stands.

Jude wore a Birmingham City shirt when he returned to St Andrew's

When Jude joined Dortmund in 2020 Birmingham retired the 17-year-old's number 22 shirt after 44 appearances.

"That was a gesture of thanks for what Jude had done," said Courtney.

"It might be wishful thinking, but I really believe Jude has unfinished business at Birmingham. I can see a scenario before he retires where he gets an opportunity to wear the number 22 again."

Should the Bellingham brothers play together against Croatia, they will become the first siblings to appear for England since Gary and Phil Neville against Spain in a friendly at Old Trafford in 2007.

It will be an immensely proud moment for their parents, Mark and Denise.

"We've played together for so long in the street and to play with my brother Jobe for England would be the biggest dream of my life," Jude, a Champions League and La Liga winner with Real Madrid, wrote on social media, external in 2024.

"That would mean more than any of the trophies. Nothing would even get close to that... nothing."

BBC reporter John Watson has been finding out why Bellingham is proving so popular with football fans across the world

#905. Grimes Makes Red Carpet Debut With Producer Elijah Weinkauf

Grimes and music producer Elijah Weinkauf made their red carpet debut at the Nov. 12 Los Angeles premiere of Blade Runner 2099, holding hands as they posed for photos.

The “Oblivion” singer (real name Clair Boucher) confirmed her romance with music producer Elijah Weinkauf Nov. 12 as they made their red carpet debut at the Los Angeles premiere of Blade Runner 2099.

The duo hit all the right notes as they posed for cameras, with Grimes looking chic for their date night, wearing a striped black and camo green dress with long sleeves and an over-sized collar. The 38-year-old completed her look with pink glasses and pointed black and pink loafers. Weinkauf—who produces music under the name VADAKIN—looked dapper in an all black suit over a black dress shirt, finishing off the outfit with brown flip-flop sandals.

While neither Grimes nor Weinkauf has publicly commented on their relationship, the two have been dating for “some time,” according to multiple outlets. Weinkauf also co-produced the “Genesis” singer’s upcoming album PSYOPERA.

Prior to her romance with the music producer, Grimes had been dating Italian DJ Anyma, although the two reportedly split in August 2025 after going public with their romance in 2024.

The “Realiti” singer was also in an on-again, off-again relationship with Tesla founder Elon Musk—with whom she shares kids X Æ A-Xii, 6, Exa Dark Sideræl, 4, and Techno Mechanicus, 4—although the two finally called it quits in March 2022 after four years.

And while Grimes has never shied away from the spotlight, she has been careful with how much she shares about her children.

"I try to never talk abt or show my kids because they deserve the right to anonymity but i just have to say their pure aura is unmatched," Grimes wrote on X in January. "Might be biased but this seems unusual."

She also admitted that she and Musk have different views on how much to share publicly about their kids.

"I have tried begging the public and my kids dad to keep them offline, and I've tried legal recourse," she shared on X in March 2025. "The state of my children's lives being public is of grave concern to me and I think about how to solve this every day. It's insane to me that theres no way to deal with this."

#904. ‘No one is unbeatable’: Tuchel eager for England to impose style on Spain

Manager calls Sunday’s Nations League decider a ‘final’ as preparations for Euro 2028 ratchet up a level

Proof of concept. It is Thomas Tuchel’s latest buzz phrase. The England manager has dropped it into the conversation pretty regularly since the Friday of last week when he named his squad for this international window, the one that was always going to decide whether his team finished first or second in their Nations League group.

By it, Tuchel means a test of his methods, what he is trying to build – or, more accurately, fine-tune – as he turns his gaze towards Euro 2028 and tries to move on from the devastation of the World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina. The test does not come any bigger than the one which faces him and his players in Madrid on Sunday night.

England ticked off part one of the mission at Wembley on Thursday when they defeated Croatia 2-1. Now for the serious business: Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium. The win over Croatia ensured that England retained a puncher’s chance of top spot, which would in theory bring easier opposition in the two-leg quarter-finals in March. Victory over the world and European champions – nothing less – would secure it owing to England’s superior goal difference.

Tuchel is calling it a “final” and he wants this. “Yeah, push our limits, see where we are,” he said. Remember England’s previous Nations League campaign when they were in the second tier? The team learned little from the ties against the Republic of Ireland, Finland and Greece – except that it was unwise of Lee Carsley, the interim manager, to jam in all of the glamour No 10s against Greece at Wembley. The matches did not help England in their preparations for the World Cup.

This is different because Spain are the country to beat. They have lost only once in 43 games and that was on penalties to Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final. Technically, it went down as a draw (even if nobody thinks it was) and so Spain’s run, which began in March 2024, is considered (by some) the longest unbeaten in men’s international history. Since they drew 0-0 with Cape Verde in their opening World Cup group game, they have won 12 straight, including all five of their Nations League matches.

Tuchel, his staff, the players and the Football Association regard the Nations League as a springboard into the Euros when England will co-host. They are desperate to reach the four-team finals tournament next June because it would ensure continued high-grade opposition. And they are desperate to lift the trophy, mainly because winning is a good habit. It is easy to feel that England’s fans are not as invested. Expect that to change if the team advance to the finals, especially if those games were in England, which would be a possibility.

Tuchel has re-geared his personnel this season, partly because of injuries but not entirely. He had only 11 players from the World Cup in his squad against Croatia; two more – Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence – hope to return against Spain after injury niggles. The manager is using different players, most notably Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ben White, Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha. Lewis-Skelly is back from a one-game ban against Spain. Scott is out injured; it felt significant that he was at Wembley to watch the Croatia game. Tuchel wants to keep him close.

Tuchel’s main tactical tweak has been to give Jude Bellingham greater licence to drift from the No 10 role, to overload on either side, to run on intuition. But it is not only Bellingham. Others have been encouraged to push into out-of-the-ordinary zones, including the full-backs. It is no longer a positional team approach. The idea is that it is freer, more fluid. Tuchel is obsessed with finding ways to accelerate the play through midfield.

The principles remain. Aggression, physicality, working hard on the cover. Intensity, including when pressing high. Are England the most economical team? No. Tuchel is aware of this. He just wants to go for it and see whether his England can impose their style on Spain. It was the same when they played them at Wembley in the Nations League opener and there were good periods before Spain ran out 3-2 winners. This time, Tuchel wants more.

“It’s not a must-win game if you go to Spain,” he said. “But the mindset is important. Beating Croatia so we could have this match was the first step and now it’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home [against Spain] – attack them, try to make it a physical game, impose our strength. And we will. I’m very confident about that.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Tuchel felt England deserved more from the topsy-turvy match against Spain at Wembley when his team conceded early and were almost overwhelmed in the first 35 minutes. They stabilised and went 2-1 up before the game turned when Harry Kane missed a penalty for 3-1.

“Once we got our energy going and played with this for the equaliser for 1-1, we were strong,” Tuchel said. “Harry’s penalty was maybe the key moment for us because we were very strong then and deserved to be 3-1 up. It would have been very difficult for Spain to come back against us. We had too many big individual mistakes in our own half on the night.

“But honestly, if you deeply look into the [Nations League] matches … Spain had some crucial ball losses against Croatia [in Split] and got away with it. They conceded some big, big chances and still managed to win in the end [with an 88th-minute Mikel Merino winner]. So no one is unbeatable. We’re full of confidence. It’s exactly what we wanted. We feel that we have something to take that we lost the last time.”

Tuchel was tetchy at the beginning of the first Nations League window in September, the wounds still raw from the criticism after the Argentina defeat. Everyone was on egg shells. The mood has greatly improved and Tuchel is back to his old self; eyes twinkling, in control. He was asked whether England had come a long way since the summer.

“Yeah, I think we’re there,” Tuchel said. “We’re ready to win on Sunday. I know what it takes and while no one can ever guarantee it, I think it’s the moment to check how far we are. And proof of concept.”
